title: Daily Do List wire protocol
description: Every REST body and WebSocket message exchanged with the daemon. Requests reject unknown keys; responses and events may gain keys (clients must ignore them).

TaskAgentStatus.description: Lifecycle of the agent's work on one to-do item (drives the badge next to the task).

notePath.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

date.description: Local ISO date when the note is a daily note.

summary.description: One-line status shown inline in the editor.

anyOf.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

unread.description: Agent messages the user has not seen yet.

anchor.description: Present when the thread is attached to a non-task line (taskId is then the anchor id, text the line): clients highlight that line.

TaskAgentRecord.description: Everything a client needs to render the agent badge for one task line.

RiskLevel.description: Safety evaluator's risk estimate for an action.

ActionCategory.description: Coarse effect category used by the safety evaluator and shown on approval cards.

ApprovalScope.description: How far an approval reaches: this call, the rest of this task, or always.

ApprovalDecision.description: The user's answer to an approval request.

id.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

anyOf.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

input.description: Tool arguments exactly as the agent proposed them.

reason.description: Why the safety evaluator wants a human in the loop.

scope.description: Scope the user granted when approving.

ApprovalRequest.description: A risky action paused by the safety gate until the user decides.

ArtifactKind.description: How a client should render an artifact.

id.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

path.description: Vault-relative sidecar path of the artifact body.

ArtifactMeta.description: An agent-produced file attached to a thread (bytes via `GET /api/artifacts/:threadId/:artifactId`).

MessageAuthor.description: Who wrote a thread message: `you`, `orchestrator`, `system` or `subagent:<name>`.

streaming.description: True while tokens are still streaming in (see `thread.delta`).

TextMessage.description: Markdown text from the agent, the user or the system.

ToolCallStatus.description: `blocked`: the safety gate refused the call.

resultPreview.description: Short, UI-safe preview of the result.

ToolCallMessage.description: A tool call made by an agent, updated in place as it runs.

approvalId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

ApprovalMessage.description: Marks where in the thread an approval was requested.

artifactId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

ArtifactMessage.description: Marks where in the thread an artifact was created.

StatusMessage.description: A task status change, with an optional note.

ThreadMessage.description: One entry of a task thread, discriminated by `kind`.

SurfaceKind.description: A live visual surface a thread can expose.

snippet.description: A sentence or two from the search result or the page.

CitedSource.description: A web page an agent found or read, as a citation preview.

OrchestratorThreadId.description: The id of the orchestrator's own chat: a thread with `taskId` and `notePath` null that records each orchestrator turn (a `status` line saying what woke it, its streamed text, its tool calls, whose inputs carry the `taskId` they act on) and takes the user's direct messages (`POST /api/threads/:id/messages`). Its status is `working` during a turn, `idle` otherwise.

id.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

anyOf.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

title.description: Task text snapshot (kept in sync as the task is edited).

routineId.description: Set on a routine's runs: the routine (`Routine.id`) this thread is one run of. Clients list these under their routine, not in the task inbox.

sources.description: Web pages the thread cites, with what the agent saw of them: clients preview citations from here, never by fetching.

Thread.description: A task's full conversation: messages, artifacts and live surfaces. The orchestrator's own chat is a thread too (see `OrchestratorThreadId`).

id.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

anyOf.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

title.description: Task text snapshot (kept in sync as the task is edited).

routineId.description: Set on a routine's runs: the routine (`Routine.id`) this thread is one run of. Clients list these under their routine, not in the task inbox.

ThreadSummary.description: A thread without its messages, for lists and badges.

RoutineNotify.description: When a finished run notifies: `always`, `when_changed` (only when it found something new) or `never`. The file spells `when_changed` as `when changed`.

RoutineUse.description: A capability a routine's runs get (its file's `uses`).

RoutineRunTrigger.description: What started a run: its schedule, a slot missed while the Mac slept or the daemon was down (`catch_up`, once however many were missed), or the user (`manual`).

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

summary.description: One line: the run's badge text.

changed.description: Whether the run found something new since the previous one.

RoutineRun.description: One run of a routine; its thread holds the conversation.

id.description: Stable id derived from the file's path (`rtn_…`).

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

schedule.description: The schedule as written in the file.

scheduleText.description: The schedule in words; absent when it can't be read.

nextRunAt.description: Absent while paused, invalid or unscheduled.

extraRunsLeft.description: Runs that may still start today beyond the schedule.

Routine.description: A standing job the agent runs on a schedule: the file `Routines/<name>.md` (schedule, notify, uses and paused in its frontmatter, the instructions as its body) plus the scheduler's state.

RoutineTemplate.description: A starter routine offered by “New routine”.

routineId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

body.description: The run's result in a line or two.

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

RoutineNotification.description: A finished run to tell the user about (sent according to the routine's `notify`).

SurfaceFrameAction.description: The action that produced a frame, for overlays (x/y in frame pixels).

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

SurfaceFrame.description: One frame of a live surface (browser screencast or desktop screenshot).

vimrc.description: Vim startup ex commands, one per line; lines starting with `"` are comments.

folder.description: Vault folder for the notes; empty = vault root.

format.description: Moment-style file name format; may contain `/` for nested folders.

template.description: Template note path; empty = no template.

DailyNoteSettings.description: Where daily notes live (mirrors Obsidian's daily-notes config).

folder.description: Vault folder for the notes; empty = vault root.

format.description: Moment-style file name format; may contain `/` for nested folders.

template.description: Template note path; empty = no template.

AgentWatchWindow.description: Days around today whose daily notes the orchestrator watches.

AgentHarnessKind.description: What runs the orchestrator and subagent conversations: `pi` (the Pi coding-agent SDK on the OpenRouter `model`) or `cursor` (the Cursor CLI's agent on `cursorModel`, signed in with the user's Cursor account).

ApprovalPolicy.description: When agents ask before acting: `ask_every_action` (every action that changes something), `ask_risky` (what the safety check flags; the default), `ask_high_risk` (only high-risk actions) or `run_everything` (never). Actions the safety check denies stay blocked under every policy.

enabled.description: Master switch: when false the orchestrator ignores note changes.

settleMs.description: Quiet period after the last edit to a task before the orchestrator looks at it.

approvalTimeoutMs.description: How long an approval request waits before it is auto-denied.

model.description: OpenRouter model id for the orchestrator and subagents with the Pi harness.

cursorModel.description: Model for the orchestrator and subagents with the Cursor harness (`claude-opus-5-5`, `composer-2.5`). The CLI's agent mode runs one preset per model; a variant id from `agent models` (`claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`) runs as its model's preset.

judgeModel.description: OpenRouter model id for the safety judge (whichever harness runs the agent).

AppSettings.description: All user settings (stored in the vault sidecar so they travel with the vault).

vimrc.description: Vim startup ex commands, one per line; lines starting with `"` are comments.

VaultEntry.description: A visible file or folder of the vault (hidden paths are never listed).

VaultTreeResponse.description: Every visible file and folder of the vault.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

version.description: Send back as `baseVersion` for optimistic concurrency.

baseVersion.description: Version edited from; `null` = create only (409 if it exists); omit to overwrite.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

WriteNoteResponse.description: The written note's canonical path and new version.

RenameRequest.description: Renames a note, or a folder with everything inside it when `from` is a folder.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

RenameResponse.description: A renamed note answers like a write; a renamed folder reports how many files moved.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

TrashResponse.description: Deletes are soft: the note or folder moved into the vault's `.trash/` folder.

ThreadActionResponse.description: 200 when the runtime finished the action; 202 with `pending: true` when it continues in the background.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

version.description: Send back as `baseVersion` for optimistic concurrency.

created.description: True when this request created the note.

DailyNoteResponse.description: A daily note, created from the template when requested.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

SearchHit.description: `name`: the note's name matched (line 0); `content`: the 0-based `line` matched.

ComputerHostApp.description: The app macOS attributes the daemon's privacy permissions to (the Daily Do List app, or the terminal or editor it runs from).

accessibility.description: Input and reading other apps' UI.

screenRecording.description: Screenshots. macOS applies a new grant after the host app restarts.

appControl.description: The `ddl-computer` helper is available; otherwise computer use is screen-level only.

hostApp.description: Absent when it can't be determined.

ComputerAccess.description: Computer use on this Mac: its two privacy permissions and whether agents can operate apps in the background.

computerAccess.description: Present where computer use exists (macOS with computer use enabled).

ExecutionStatus.description: The execution provider and what it can do.

problem.description: Why the agent cannot run, when it can't.

AgentStatusResponse.description: The agent runtime's state (also pushed as `agent.status`).

TaskRecordsResponse.description: The agent records of one note's tasks.

ThreadResponse.description: A full thread and every approval requested in it.

PostMessageRequest.description: A user reply in a thread. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; it must not be empty.

RoutineListResponse.description: Every routine (sorted by name) and the starter templates for “New routine”.

CreateRoutineRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/routines`: a new routine file `Routines/<name>.md`. The daemon checks the name (a file name) and the schedule (400 with the reason when it can't be read).

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

RoutineRunResponse.description: A run started now: the routine and the run's thread.

SyncTargetKind.description: `none`, `local` (another folder), `s3`, or `remote` (the sync service shared with other devices).

lastSyncedAt.description: When the last pass finished; null before it.

pendingChanges.description: Files changed on either side and not synced yet.

items.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

conflicts.description: Conflict copies waiting to be resolved.

deviceName.description: This device's name as other devices see it (`remote` only).

ComputerPermissionPane.description: A System Settings privacy pane computer use needs.

ApiErrorCode.description: Machine-readable error code. Treat unknown codes like any failure with that HTTP status.

ConflictResponse.description: 409 of a note write or rename whose target changed; `current` is null if the note is gone.

ApprovalConflictResponse.description: 409 of an approval decision when the approval is no longer pending.

VaultChangeOrigin.description: Who changed the vault: another program, a client (see `clientId`), the agent, or sync.

path.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

WsErrorCode.description: Machine-readable reason of a server `error` event.

clientId.description: Client id chosen by the client.

VaultChangedEvent.description: Vault paths changed (coalesced). Clients skip batches carrying their own `clientId`.

notePath.description: Canonical vault-relative path (no leading `/`, `.`/`..` or empty segments).

TaskRecordsEvent.description: Snapshot of a note's task records.

ThreadUpsertEvent.description: A thread was created or its summary changed.

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

ThreadMessageEvent.description: A message was added or replaced (same `id`) in a thread.

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

ThreadDeltaEvent.description: Streaming text appended to a `streaming` text message (droppable; the final message repairs gaps).

ApprovalUpsertEvent.description: An approval request was created or decided.

threadId.description: Runtime id, safe to use in URLs.

SurfaceFrameEvent.description: A live surface frame; only sent to clients subscribed to that thread's surface (droppable).

RoutinesChangedEvent.description: Every routine, whenever one changed (its file, its schedule, its last run).

RoutineNotificationEvent.description: A routine's run finished and its `notify` says to tell the user (clients show a notification).

ServerErrorEvent.description: Something the client sent was rejected (or the connection is about to close).

ServerEvent.description: Every server → client WebSocket message, discriminated by `type`.

clientId.description: Client id chosen by the client.

apiVersion.description: API_VERSION the client was built against; absent = 1 (legacy clients).

ClientHelloEvent.description: First message a client sends: its id and the API version it speaks.

SurfaceSubscribeEvent.description: Start receiving `surface.frame` events for a thread's surface.

SurfaceUnsubscribeEvent.description: Stop receiving frames for a thread's surface.

ThreadReadEvent.description: The user has seen a thread (clears its unread count).

EditorActivityEvent.description: Where the user is typing, so the orchestrator never jumps on a half-written task.

ClientEvent.description: Every client → server WebSocket message, discriminated by `type`.
